hints.title: Order Inversion in FIFO Channels
hints.text: A last-in first-out interface must be constructed using only standard first-in first-out operations. How can rotating newly appended elements place the newest item at the front?

hints.title: Single-Queue Push Rotation
hints.text: When pushing a new element x, append x to the back of the queue. Then immediately dequeue and re-enqueue all preceding elements so x sits at the front.

hints.title: Constant-Time Pop and Top
hints.text: Because each push rotates the buffer so the latest element is frontmost, pop and top operations simply read and remove from the queue head in constant time.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.time: O(N) for push, O(1) for pop, top, empty
variables: N: number of elements currently stored in the stack
complexity.notes: Push rotates N - 1 elements so the newest entry is positioned for O(1) popping.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Attempting to reverse elements during pop requires two queues and copies data on every read.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A single deque avoids allocating a second collection while achieving O(1) reads.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Ability to implement the stack with only one queue rather than two.

solutions.approach: Single-queue push rotation placing newest item at head
